newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australia bonds hold firm, activity low key.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australia bonds hold firm, activity low key.

text.p: *Australian bond yields finished lower, but activity was fairly subdued with U.S. Treasuries closed for Columbus Day and having fully factored in the expectation a local rate easing.
*This week's RBA quarterly bulletin likely to be key event.

Australian bond yields finished lower, but activity was fairly subdued with U.S. Treasuries closed for Columbus Day and as the market has already fully factored in the expectation of a local interest rate easing.

Traders said the market opened up with a bid tone which took bond futures to their highest level in over 2-1/2 years, but the market is expected to find further gains difficult until it sees the widely expected cut in current 7.0 percent interest rates.
This is seen most likely to occur at the next Reserve Bank board meeting on November 5 and after the central bank sees next week's quarterly inflation and wages data.
In the meantime the market will be eagerly awaiting this week's Reserve Bank quarterly bulletin for any insight into its thinking on the economy.

"The big danger for the market from that will be any comments along the lines that the economy is going along as they (the RBA) expect given that the front-end has adopted such an aggressive stance in terms of an easing," one trader said.
Indeed the December bill futures contract ended at 93.55, indicating a cash rate of 6.45 percent at maturity, while the March 1997 position at 93.66 is pointing to a bill rate of 6.34 percent.

A firm close in U.S. bonds on Friday after a modest rise in the September U.S. PPI provided the local market with the early firm tone which took the cash 10-year bond yield close to 7.50 percent at one stage.
The December 10-year bond futures contract touched 92.480 just after the opening, taking it to the highest level for a front position in dayside trade since March 1994.
However, it failed to progress to the 92.560 level seen briefly in after hours trading just over a week ago following the U.S. payrolls report.

The Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread remained sub-100 basis points, a level breached on Friday, despite the market's low-key activity. However, New Zealand's premium narrowed sharply as bonds there rallied after this weekend's election, even though the result remains uncertain.

The 10-year bond contract breached 92.440 resistance at the opening, but is expected to find the psychological 92.500 level a stiff barrier en route to the 92.560 high seen in the October 4 SYCOM session.
